**2026-10-27.** A patch release with one fix: a resumed step that the engine refuses to commit now
fails the instance, once. Before, it was retried every few seconds, forever. Everything in the v0.6.0
release notes applies. There is no `q:` namespace change and no migration, and the
snapshot format is unchanged, so an instance parked by a 0.6.1 engine resumes under 0.6.2.

## Fixed: a refused send after an early reply re-ran forever

`<q:reply continue="true">` answers the caller first and finishes the flow afterwards. The reply is
sent, the instance parks with a timer that is due at once, and the timer poller resumes it to run
everything after the reply. When the caller's channel runs `ack-mode: on-persist`, that reply is
the body of a `202 Accepted`.

Before a resumed step commits, the engine runs its own checks. One of them reads back every
`<q:send>` with the codec it states and refuses a message that breaks that codec's contract
(`SUTRA.OUTBOUND.VALIDATION_REJECT`), so an invalid message never leaves. The refusal itself was
correct. What went wrong was what happened to the instance afterwards. On a timer resume, the
refusal was handled like a database error. The step was never marked FAILED, and the poller pushed
the timer out by its 5-second backoff and fired it again, with no limit. Each fire re-ran the tail
up to the refused send, repeating its audit events, its logs and any external call a task made,
while the instance stayed SUSPENDED at the reply node and nothing after the send was ever armed.

A continue-reply flow is where this showed up, because its whole tail runs on a timer resume. A
timer catch event, a timer boundary and a `<q:retry>` backoff re-drive went through the same path.
On a relay resume the instance was not failed either: the error went back to the sender, and a
broker redelivered the message indefinitely.

In 0.6.2 a step the engine refuses to commit fails the instance the way a failing task does:

- the instance is persisted as FAILED with the refusal's code, which
  `GET /sutra/instances/{id}` shows as `failureCode`;
- its wait and timer rows are resolved in the same step, so nothing fires again, and a later
  relay is told the instance is FAILED (`SUTRA.DISPATCH.INSTANCE_FAILED`);
- listeners receive one `INSTANCE_FAILED`, which is the audit journal's entry and the event an
  `on-complete` acknowledgement settles on;
- the refused message never reaches the outbox.

The same holds when a relay's reply cannot render, or when a wait the step parks has a `<q:alias>`
that cannot be evaluated. A database error while committing is not a refusal. It leaves the
instance where it was and is retried exactly as before.

The fix has tests at two levels. In-process, against the dispatcher, for each resume path:
the continue-reply tail, a timer catch, a retry re-drive and a relay. Each one checks that the
instance fails once, that a second fire or redelivery runs nothing, and that a database error on
the same step still leaves the instance for the retry. In a container, against the engine image
and PostgreSQL: an on-persist flow answers 202, then fails at its send. The test checks that the
instance shows FAILED with the code, that the audit journal has one `INSTANCE_FAILED`, that the
tail ran once across several backoff periods, and that the outbox holds nothing.

## Upgrading

Replace the image or the binary. Nothing in a deployment package needs to change. An instance
that an older engine left stuck this way is still SUSPENDED in the store. After the upgrade, its
next timer fire fails it as described above.

## Install

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/startr-trade/sutra:0.6.2
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/startr-trade/sutra/main/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --version v0.6.2
```

The library crates are on crates.io as `sutra-feel = "0.6.2"` and `sutra-dmn = "0.6.2"`.
